quote: CC Chemokines in a Tumor: A Review of Pro-Cancer and Anti-Cancer Properties of the Ligands of Receptors CCR1, CCR2, CCR3, and CCR4.
summary: Cancer-focused review of CC chemokine ligands of CCR1 and other receptors, with no new data and nothing on UC.

quote: Small-molecule inhibitors, chemokine and chemokine receptor-deficient mice, antibodies and modified chemokines are the current tools available for CCL5 research, and there are several ongoing clinical trials targeting the CCL5 receptors, CCR1, CCR3 and CCR5.
summary: Review of CCL5 as a therapeutic target that notes clinical trials targeting its receptors including CCR1; no new data.
Review of plant anti-inflammatory compounds where CCR1 appears only in an abbreviation list.

quote: Abundant expression of CCR1, CXCR4, and CCR5 was found in all forms of arthritis, with a specific increase of CCL5 and CCL15 in RA.
summary: CCR1 is abundantly expressed in synovial tissue across arthritis types, with altered expression on blood cells; the disease is arthritis, not UC.

quote: Genome-wide association studies have identified associations with genome-wide significance (P < 5 × 10(-8)) in the IL23R-IL12RB2, IL10, STAT4, CCR1-CCR3, KLRC4, ERAP1, TNFAIP3, and FUT2 loci.
summary: Review of Behcet's disease immunogenetics noting the CCR1-CCR3 locus as a GWAS hit; no new data and no UC.

quote: Administration on days 7 through 14 after trinitrobenzene sulfonic acid administration of a CCR1/CCR5 receptor antagonist, Met-RANTES, resulted in a significant reduction of both macroscopic and microscopic colonic damage, as well as reducing the recruitment into the colon of monocytes, mast cells, and neutrophils.
summary: In rat TNBS colitis, CCR1 expression rose in the chronic phase and the CCR1/CCR5 antagonist Met-RANTES reduced colonic damage and leukocyte recruitment.

quote: CCR1, by virtue of specific expression in Abeta plaques, may be a marker for Alzheimer pathology.
summary: Review of chemokines in neurological disease noting CCR1 expression in amyloid plaques as a possible Alzheimer marker; no UC content.

quote: To determine whether chemokine receptors are expressed in human colonic epithelium, HT-29 cells were examined by RT-PCR for the expression of the chemokine receptors for lymphotactin, fractalkine, CCR1-10, and CXCR1-5.
summary: CCR1 was one of many chemokine receptors screened in HT-29 cells; only CXCR4 was consistently detected, so no CCR1-specific finding.

quote: In the current study of Behçet disease (BD), nonsynonymous variants (NSVs) identified by deep exonic resequencing of 10 genes found by GWAS (IL10, IL23R, CCR1, STAT4, KLRK1, KLRC1, KLRC2, KLRC3, KLRC4, and ERAP1) and 11 genes selected for their role in innate immunity (IL1B, IL1R1, IL1RN, NLRP3, MEFV, TNFRSF1A, PSTPIP1, CASP1, PYCARD, NOD2, and TLR4) were evaluated for BD association.
summary: CCR1 was one of many genes resequenced in Behcet disease; only IL23R and TLR4 showed rare-variant association, with no CCR1 result.

quote: Quantitative gene expression analysis of a panel of 92 genes linked to inflammatory signaling pathway revealed down-regulation of the expression of 14 pro-inflammatory genes (TLR1, TLR2, TLR4, TLR8, TRAF5, TRAF6, TNFSF18, IL6R, IL23, CCR1, CCR4, CCL17, STAT3, MAP3K1) by the lipid extracts.
summary: CCR1 is one of 14 genes down-regulated by algal lipid extracts in LPS-stimulated THP-1 macrophages, with no CCR1-specific analysis.

quote: Macrophage-specific PPAR-γ deletion significantly exacerbated clinical activity and colonic pathology, impaired the splenic and mesenteric lymph node regulatory T-cell compartment, increased percentages of lamina propria (LP) CD8+ T cells, increased surface expression of CD40, Ly6C, and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR-4) in LP macrophages, and upregulated expression of colonic IFN-γ, CXCL9, CXCL10, IL-22, IL1RL1, CCR1, suppressor of cytokine signaling 3, and MHC class II in mice with IBD.
summary: Colonic CCR1 was among several genes upregulated when macrophage PPAR-gamma was deleted in experimental colitis; no CCR1-specific analysis.

quote: The data suggest that the targeting of Th1-associated chemokine receptors reduce joint inflammation, bone destruction, and cell recruitment into joints with AIA.
summary: Met-RANTES, antagonising CCR1 and CCR5, reduced joint inflammation, bone erosion and macrophage and neutrophil recruitment in rat arthritis (not colitis).

quote: We also found that variants near STAT4, IL10, and CCR1-CCR3 were significant susceptibility loci for PFAPA, suggesting that the pathogenesis of PFAPA involves abnormal antigen-presenting cell function and T cell activity and polarization, thereby implicating both innate and adaptive immune responses at the oropharyngeal mucosa.
summary: Variants near the CCR1-CCR3 locus were significant susceptibility loci for PFAPA syndrome; no direction stated and not UC.
Paper studies CCL23 expression in nasal polyps; CCR1 is mentioned only as its receptor, with no CCR1 data.

quote: In turn, CCL3 attracted inflammatory monocytes via their chemokine receptor CCR1, which was indispensable for their recruitment into the inflamed gut.
summary: In mouse T. gondii ileitis, CCR1 was needed to recruit inflammatory monocytes into the inflamed gut, amplifying intestinal inflammation; preliminary link to Crohn's disease.

quote: Stimulation of cells with CCL5 increased CCR5 but not CCR1 and CCR3 expression.
summary: In osteosarcoma cells CCL5 did not change CCR1 expression; the study focuses on CCR5 and is unrelated to UC.

quote: The increased sensitivity was accompanied by enhanced mRNA expression of proinflammatory cytokines (TNFalpha, IL-6, IFN-gamma, IL-12p35, IL-23p19, and IL-17), chemokines (MCP-1/CCL2, MIP-1alpha/CCL3, and RANTES/CCL5), and chemotactic factor receptors (CCR1, CCR2, and CCR5), but downregulation of the anti-inflammatory cytokines (IL-4, IL-10, and TGF-beta) in the spinal cord.
summary: CCR1 mRNA was one of many genes raised in the spinal cord of PACAP-deficient mice with EAE; no CCR1-specific result.

quote: CCR1 inhibition with Met-RANTES attenuated neuroinflammation, thereby reducing brain edema and improving neurobehavioral functions.
summary: In mouse intracerebral hemorrhage, CCR1 inhibition reduced neuroinflammation and edema while CCR1 activation by CCL5 worsened deficits (brain, not colitis).

quote: Allo-SCT with CCR1(-/-) donor cells significantly reduced systemic and target organ GVHD severity, and CCR1 expression on both T cells and accessory cells contributed to GVHD mortality.
summary: CCR1-deficient donor cells reduced graft-versus-host disease severity and T-cell responses in mice, so CCR1 promotes GVHD (not colitis).

quote: Moreover, inhibition of C-C chemokine receptor 1 (CCR1, the receptor of CCL6) in tumor cells reduces tumor cell migration and metastasis.
summary: CCR1 inhibition in tumour cells reduced migration and metastasis driven by eosinophil-derived CCL6; no colitis outcome for CCR1.

quote: Notably, three causal risk genes of CCR1, CXCR6, and ABO were highly expressed in these three cell types, respectively.
summary: Integrating GWAS with single-cell data identified CCR1 as a causal risk gene for severe COVID-19, highly expressed in CD16+ monocytes; not UC.

quote: TNF-α-primed-hMSCs secrete high level of CCL5, which interacts with its receptor CCR1 expressed in colon cancer cells.
summary: CCR1 is expressed in colon cancer cells and mediates MSC-derived CCL5 signalling in a colorectal cancer progression model; CCR1 was not itself perturbed and UC was not studied.

quote: We show here that ribavirin reduces mortality, from 100% to 10 and 30%, respectively, in gene-deleted CCR1(-/-) mice and in wild-type mice treated with the small-molecule chemokine receptor antagonist, Met-RANTES.
summary: CCR1 deletion or antagonism with Met-RANTES plus ribavirin sharply reduced mortality in mouse pneumovirus infection (lung infection, not colitis).

quote: In contrast, hepatic RNA-Seq analysis identified increased expression of MHC class II genes, as well as chemokines and chemokine receptors involved in macrophage recruitment (Ccr1, Ccr5, Ccl5, Cx3cr1), consistent with hepatic F4/80 labeling and macrophage infiltration into the liver.
summary: Hepatic Ccr1 was among several macrophage-recruitment genes raised by TCDD in mouse liver; no Ccr1-specific analysis and not UC.

quote: F. prausnitzii exhibits anti-inflammatory effects on cellular and TNBS colitis models, partly due to secreted metabolites able to block NF-kappaB activation and IL-8 production.
summary: F. prausnitzii secreted metabolites reduced IL-8 production in cell models; IL-8 was a readout, not directly perturbed.
